files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
### Added
- **Colour settings for money in and money out.** Settings has a new Colours section with a colour-blind friendly preset (blue and orange) or your own colours, picked separately for the light and dark theme. They are used across amounts, budget bars, charts and PDF exports, and each person sets their own. Default keeps the colours as they are now. Reported by @trucks192 ([#432](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/432))
- **Link a transaction to a bill.** A transaction's menu has **Link to bill…**, which files it as one of the bill's payments without moving the bill's due date, so a payment you typed in yourself, or one left behind by a bill you deleted and set up again, shows in Bills by Month. Bills with the same name are listed with their dates, and the ones matching the amount come first. **Unlink from bill** takes it off again, apart from the bill's latest payment, which Mark Unpaid on the bill undoes. Only money going out of the bill's own account can be linked. Reported by @TerjeTM ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))

### Changed
- **Translations.** German and French have been updated from Weblate, and the Italian translation has grown from a handful of strings to about 300.
- **A transfer whose other side was deleted counts as spending until it is linked again.** An older version could delete one side of a transfer and leave the other pointing at it. Updating lets go of the missing side, so the one left can be matched to its other side again, and until it is, reports count it like any other payment.

### Fixed
- **The amber warning dot on accounts shows its colour.** A Nextcloud style overrode it, so the dot beside an account with a warning, and the one on the account's own page, came out as a faint tint and, on the account page, a rounded square. Both now show the full warning colour as a round dot.
- **Switching a paid bill to One-Time keeps it paid.** A Custom or monthly bill switched to One-Time on a date it had already paid came back overdue with Mark Paid, and pressing it paid the bill a second time. It now stays paid, Mark Unpaid still works on it, and its reminders are taken down. Recurring income switched the same way stays received. A one-time date after the occurrence the last payment paid, such as a final invoice, is still due. Reported by @TerjeTM ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Mark Paid asks before paying something twice.** When a bill already has a payment for the date it is due, Mark Paid says so before anything else and offers **Use that payment**, which marks it paid on that payment's date without recording anything new, or **Record another payment**. Mark Received does the same for income. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **A double click can't pay a bill twice.** Two clicks on Mark Paid, Skip or Mark Received that arrived together both went through, booking the payment twice and moving the bill on by two dates. Only the first one counts now, the buttons are disabled while it runs, and a Skip names the date the page showed. A double click no longer answers the dialog it opens either, nor changes the choice in it, and Enter in a question such as Mark Unpaid no longer goes ahead once a stray click has moved the focus off its buttons. When one of these buttons is refused, for instance in a tab left open since the bill was paid, the list reloads to show where the bill is now. Undo after a Skip only puts back a date the bill was due on. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Paid Custom bills stay paid until their next date.** A Custom bill paid for its month showed Mark Paid again 31 days later, which paid the next year's date. Its row now goes by its own months, and a one-time bill no longer shows a "next due" date. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Income received a day early is no longer waiting for it.** Before 3.0, Mark Received on money that came in before its expected date recorded it but left the income expecting it, so the Income page showed it overdue and Mark Received recorded it again. Updating moves those on to their next date, and Repair Data lists any a restored backup brings back under **Income Received Early but Still Expected**. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Repair Data finds more payments recorded twice.** Older versions could book a bill's payment twice when a pre-booked transaction went through on its date and the bill was then marked paid. Repair Data now also finds these when the bill is a transfer (both sides are removed together, and only where you can change both accounts), when the bill has since been deleted, when its amount changed between the two, and on a bill usually paid a few days early. For a one-time bill paid twice it offers the newer payment and keeps the bill paid on the older one. Nothing is ticked for you. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Importing a CSV again with different columns doesn't add it twice.** A row only counted as already imported when the columns were mapped the same way, so mapping the description to two columns the second time brought the whole file in again. A line that matches a row an earlier import put in the account is now shown as a duplicate, while new lines from a later statement still come in. This also works when one of your import rules set the row's payee, or a rule or you changed its description, reference or payee since. The app now keeps the payee each transaction was imported with, so a payee you edit by hand after updating doesn't make the row come in again. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Bills by Month shows what was paid when.** Each payment stays in the month it was paid, so a payment made twice no longer pushes into the next month and makes that one look paid twice. A due date paid more than once shows how many times, and hovering a month lists each payment, its date and the due date it paid. A payment you link to a bill for the date it is due next pays that date, rather than showing as a second payment of the one before, and a payment made in December for a date in January, or the other way round, counts in one year only. A month a bill paid twice within a few days still shows 2× after the bill is switched to One-Time. Months the bill moved past with no payment recorded are no longer drawn crossed out like paid ones, and no longer count towards Monthly Totals, which now add up what was paid and what is still due. A bill that was paid this year and has since stopped stays under Active Only. The CSV and PDF export print what each month shows, where before they printed the bill's amount in every month. The month boxes count only the bills in their total. Reported by @TerjeTM ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **A transaction with a vendor and no description can be edited.** Mark Paid and Mark Received record their transaction with the bill's or income's name as the vendor and no description, and the edit form wouldn't save a change to one, such as a new date. A description is now only needed when there is no vendor. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **A description or vendor cut short in the transactions list shows in full when you hover it**, as does the reference under it, in the Transactions list and in an account's register. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Overdue income stands out on the Income page.** It now has the same red marker and edge as an overdue bill, and completed or inactive income looks like a paid bill. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Repair Data is easier to read.** Its counts are readable in the light theme, each tick sits on its line at a normal size, dates and amounts no longer break across lines, and a payment with no vendor goes by its description or its bill's name instead of (unnamed). ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **The Strong match badge in Mark Paid's dialog is readable in the light theme.**
- **The hints on the import's Map Columns step are no longer red.** The hints under Date, Amount and Description looked like errors, and those fields sat slightly out of line with the rest.
- **A skipped date no longer reads as paid.** After Skip, a bill, transfer or income showed its last payment with a Paid or Received badge and no buttons until its next date came round. It now shows the date it is next due. Undo after a Skip also brings Mark Unpaid back for the payment before it. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Bills by Month keeps its own settings.** The general Generate Report button set its year and account back to this year and All Accounts, and the period, account and tag filters that don't apply to it are now hidden while it is shown. The heatmap draws as soon as you switch to it, its figures are readable on the darkest months, and the bill names stay in view when the table scrolls sideways. In the CSV and PDF export the Amount column is formatted like the months, a row of several invoices with different amounts leaves it blank, and long names stay inside their column. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **The import's review step says more.** It shows the payee when one is mapped, counts against the whole file ("Showing 50 of 1000"), shows Uncategorized for a row a rule touched without setting a category, and Show uncategorized hides those rows too. The message afterwards uses the right plurals. On Map Columns the hints are small grey text with room under them. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **The transactions list keeps its Description column on a laptop screen.** With an account picked, the column shrank to nothing at 1280px and below, and in an account's register at 1024px. It now keeps room for the text and the table scrolls sideways instead, with the actions column, the page controls and the category and tag pickers staying in view, and the column headings stay at the top of a long list. In those pickers Escape now leaves the transaction as it was, where it saved the choice anyway, and the tag picker can be used from the keyboard. On a phone the filters stay inside their panel. An account's register can be sorted by Date, Description or Amount from its headings, which looked sortable but did nothing, and a click on them no longer re-sorts the Transactions list instead. Untick Balance in the column settings to give the description more room, which did nothing before. In the register the reference sits on its own line under the description, the Balance column fits its amount, and long category names end with an ellipsis. The search box filters as you type. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Easier to read in more places.** Due Soon, Expected Soon and Paid badges, Mark Paid under the pointer, Mark Received in the dark theme, the calendar icon before dates, the required-field asterisks in the transaction and import dialogs and the ticked option in the payment dialogs were all faint, and now meet the usual contrast level in both themes. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Dialogs put their close button on the title row** instead of a box on a row of its own, and Repair Data keeps Close and Fix Selected Issues in view while its list scrolls. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **Bills and income still due come first.** Paid one-time bills and finished income were listed above everything else on some databases. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **On a narrow screen the menu button gets out of the way** while you scroll down, and comes back when you scroll up. It covered whatever passed under it. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
- **After Mark Paid from the keyboard, focus stays on the bill** instead of going back to the top of the page. ([#399](https://github.com/otherworld-dev/Budget/issues/399))
